title_en: ESCAPE — WHERE MARS'S AIR WENT: MAVEN & ATMOSPHERIC LOSS
title_ru: УБЕГАНИЕ — КУДА ДЕЛСЯ ВОЗДУХ МАРСА: MAVEN И ПОТЕРЯ АТМОСФЕРЫ
description: An interactive field guide to how Mars lost its air: scale height and the exobase, Jeans escape of hydrogen, hot oxygen from recombination, ion pickup and sputtering, why gravity matters more than the missing magnetic field, NASA's MAVEN orbiter (2014–2025) and its 2–3 kg/s loss budget, solar storms, argon and deuterium isotopes, and four billion years of leak.
og: Mars leaks 2–3 kg of gas a second. Find its exobase and the Jeans flux of hydrogen, see why hot oxygen escapes Mars but not Earth, turn up a solar storm, read the loss in argon 38/36 and D/H, and run the leak back four billion years, checked against MAVEN, Curiosity, Mars Express and NASA data.
brand: ESCAPE — TECHNICAL FIELD GUIDE / ТЕХНИЧЕСКИЙ СПРАВОЧНИК
llms: How Mars lost its atmosphere: scale height and exobase, Jeans escape of hydrogen (calculator for Mars and Earth), hot oxygen from O2+ recombination versus escape energy, ion pickup and sputtering, why gravity matters more than the missing magnetic field, MAVEN's 2014–2025 loss budget (2–3 kg/s) and its loss in December 2025, solar-storm boosts, argon 38/36 and D/H Rayleigh distillation, and four billion years of loss under a brighter young Sun.

freshness.claim: MAVEN lost 6 Dec 2025, mission ended 3 Jun 2026, preliminary cause (spin drained batteries), no final root cause published as of Nov 2026
Mars Express: ESA Science Programme Committee endorsed a further extension on 10–11 June 2026, no new end date published (as of Nov 2026)
Tianwen-1 MOMAG measuring since 13 Nov 2021 (implied ongoing)
